title: In Vitro Reconstitution and Imaging of Microtubule Dynamics by Fluorescence and Label-free Microscopy
protocol: Flow 20 μl of 100 μg/ml neutravidin in 1× BRB80 into the flow chamber.
Draw the neutravidin solution through the chamber using vacuum at low power.
Wash subsequent volumes through the chamber by touching absorbent paper to one end and pipetting from the other side.
Incubate for 5 min.
Place the flow chamber inside a humidified container with a lid to avoid drying out.
Wash out neutravidin with 2 x 20 μL of 1× BRB80.
Flow 2 x 20 μL of 1% Pluronic F-127 in 1× BRB80 through the chamber and incubate for 15 to 45 min.
Wash the chamber with 2 x 20 μL of wash buffer composed of 1× BRB80 supplemented with 1 mg/mL κ-casein.
Flow in 20 μL of thawed GMPCPP-seeds diluted in wash buffer into the chamber and incubate for 5 min.
Remove unbound seeds with 2 x 20 μL wash buffer.
Mix GTP to a final concentration of 2 mM.
Add β mercaptoethanol to a final concentration of 1% v/v.
Mix κ-Casein to a final concentration of 1 mg/mL.
Mix PCA to a final concentration of 2.5 mM.
Mix PCD to a final concentration of 25 nM.
Dissolve methylcellulose to a final concentration of 0.15% w/v.
Add Trolox to a final concentration of 2 mM.
Label and/or mix tubulin in 1× BRB80.
Flow the reaction mixture through the chamber.
Seal the chamber openings with silicone vacuum grease.
Mount the sample onto the microscope.
Start imaging.
Adjust the TIRF angle to minimize background signal from soluble labeled tubulin.
Keep laser power and exposure time to a minimum to prevent photobleaching.
Flow in 20 μL anti-rhodamine antibody (20–200 μg/mL in 1× PBS) to immobilize rhodamine-labeled seeds or flow in neutravidin to immobilize biotinylated seeds.
Incubate the flow cell for 15 min at room temperature.
Wash the flow cell three times with 20 μL of 1× BRB80.
Flow in 20 μL of 1% Pluronic-F127 in 1× BRB80 and incubate for 20 min.
Wash five times with 20 μL 1× BRB80.
Warm 1× BRB80 to room temperature for moderate flow chamber temperature during GMPCPP-stabilized microtubule seed injection.
Flow 10–15 μL of diluted GMPCPP-stabilized seeds into the flow chamber using a cut-off 20 μL pipette tip and incubate for 7–10 min at room temperature.
Dilute 5 μL GMPCPP-stabilized microtubules in 30 μL prewarmed to 37°C BRB80.
Evaluate immobilized microtubule seeds on the glass surface using a microscope.
Wash with 60 μL prewarmed to 37°C BRB80.
Mix D-glucose to achieve a final concentration of 40 mM.
Add glucose oxidase to reach a final concentration of 250 nM.
Add catalase to attain a final concentration of 65 nM.
Add β-Mercaptoethanol to obtain a final concentration of 1%.
Mix κ-Casein to achieve a final concentration of 0.1 mg/mL.
Add methylcellulose to reach a final concentration of 0.1%.
Combine the mixture in 1× BRB80 buffer.
Prepare a final volume of 150–300 μL for one experiment.
Keep the reaction mixture on ice.
Centrifuge casein for 2 min at 13,000 × g before adding to the polymerization reaction.
Supplement the polymerization reaction with fresh GTP.
Wash the channel with 20 μL of polymerization reaction supplemented with GTP.
Thaw label-free tubulin quickly and put it on ice.
Spin down the label-free tubulin at 4°C and 13,000 × g for 5 min.
Dilute the label-free tubulin to the desired concentration with polymerization reaction mix complemented with GTP.
Flow the label-free tubulin into the flow cell.
Warm the objective to 34°C before starting the experiment.
Keep the temperature stable using implemented temperature control during the experiment.
Switch on any heat source overnight to prewarm and equilibrate the whole optical setup and room to a stable temperature.
Adjust the aperture and field iris for best contrast as needed.
Use as much LED power as possible without saturating the camera, typically 4% LED power.
Average 10 frames in real-time during image acquisition.
Enhance the contrast of the sample by using 90% of the total dynamic range of greyscale levels.
Adjust the focus to achieve maximal contrast for the microtubules.
Move the stage laterally sufficiently fast for a low-noise background image.
Record and median average 400 images acquired at a frame rate of 25 Hz.
Subtract the background image from any recorded image in real-time.
Record videos of microtubule dynamics.
